chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a dog touching a part of a man's body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash the place that it touched.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing if a dog touches a person's body?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *al-klab* (dogs) as *najis al-ain* (impure in essence), establishing that contact transfers impurity to the touched area. It specifies that washing the exact spot of contact is sufficient for purification, reflecting the Shia juristic view that distinguishes between the dog's inherent impurity and the requirement for full-body ablution or washing. This ruling underscores the practical application of ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily life, emphasizing precision over excessive rigor.
